questions.prompt: Which beginning-of-construction position should govern for Cottonwood Solar I: off-site transformer manufacture from December 22, 2025, or on-site physical work from January 12, 2026?
questions.context: The notice to proceed (December 18, 2025) is not physical work. On-site physical work began January 12, 2026. Off-site custom transformer manufacture under a December 10, 2025 binding contract reportedly began December 22, 2025, but the independent engineer expresses no opinion and Seller's memo has not been delivered. The choice decides whether domestic content qualifies (47.8% against a 45% or 50% threshold) and whether the FEOC material assistance rules apply.

evidence.text: Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025 and continued thereafter.
On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.

options.label: Accept off-site physical work: construction began December 22, 2025
options.consequence: Domestic content qualifies at 47.8% against the 45% threshold, and the FEOC material assistance rules do not apply. Buyer relies on the off-site method and should require counsel's memo and manufacturer records, plus continuity evidence.

options.label: On-site physical work governs: construction began January 12, 2026
options.consequence: Domestic content fails at 47.8% against the 50% threshold, so the credit rate drops to 40%. The FEOC rules apply, and compliance is unverified without the module certification and a cost ratio calculation.

options.label: Defer: treat as unresolved until Seller's memo and manufacturer records are reviewed
options.consequence: T5, T6 and T8 stay open. Make substantiation of the 2025 start a condition precedent, with a price adjustment or indemnity if it fails.

questions.prompt: How should Buyer treat the unmet apprenticeship labor-hour requirement and the pending $370,800 cure payment?
questions.context: Apprentice hours are 13.2% against the 15.0% required, with no good faith effort exception documented. The cure payment has not been made, and Seller only states that it intends to pay before placed in service. The insurance binder excludes known PWA deficiencies as of binding. If PWA fails, the 5x multiplier is lost and the credit falls sharply.

evidence.text: The labor hour requirement is not satisfied for the period reviewed. The Seller has not documented a Good Faith Effort exception for the shortfall.
At $50 per labor hour, the cure payment would be $370,800. As of the report date, the payment has not been made
Key exclusions Known prevailing wage or apprenticeship deficiencies as of binding; changes in law

options.label: Treat PWA as met only after proof of cure payment, as a condition precedent to closing
options.consequence: The 5x multiplier is preserved once IRS payment evidence and full-period compliance reporting are delivered. Buyer still needs specific indemnity, since the insurance excludes this known deficiency.

options.label: Treat PWA as not met unless and until cured
options.consequence: Price and size the deal on the base rate without the 5x multiplier, or decline to proceed.
